cards.headline: A song born from 'death techno' sessions
cards.snippet: Speaking to Apple Music about "Hey, Ma," the lead single from Bon Iver's 2019 album i, i, Justin Vernon explained that the song began in the studio with producer BJ Burton. He said about 90 percent of what the two make together is "death techno," so some tracks simply hang around unfinished. This one stayed in play while Vernon, Burton and the wider team kept working on it. It eventually became the song that felt emblematic of the whole record.
cards.context: Vernon speaking to Apple Music about making the lead single from i, i.

cards.headline: Debuted a year before release, then played as fans left
cards.snippet: Bon Iver first played "Hey, Ma" live at Bonnaroo in 2018. A year later, in June 2019, the studio version arrived in London. The band played it over the PA after their headline set at the All Points East festival, alongside another new song, "U (Man Like)." The stage screen then pointed the audience to a cryptic website, icommai.com. It led to blog posts listing collaborators, including Bruce Hornsby's circle, Moses Sumney, Bryce Dessner, Brad Cook and Psymun.
cards.context: Fans were also pointed to a cryptic website, icommai.com, listing collaborators.

cards.headline: Bon Iver as a memory from a past life
cards.snippet: With a Bon Iver song, it's like hearing your favorite song from one of your past lives for the first time in this life. The memory is hazy and faraway, but you feel the remembrance deep within you
cards.context: The top comment. It describes the hazy, déjà-vu feeling the music gives.

cards.headline: Nobody knows what it's about, everyone feels it
cards.snippet: I feel like I have no idea what any of his songs are about, yet my emotions are directly impacted. He portrays his message through melody, arrangement, and sound.
